ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The square $A B C D$ has side length $3 \mathrm{~cm}$. The points $M$ and $N$, which lie on the sides $A D$ and $A B$ respectively, are joined to the corner $C$. That way the square is split up into three parts with equal area. How long is the line segment DM?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows square ABCD with D at the top-left, C at the top-right, B at the bottom-right, and A at the bottom-left. Point M lies on side AD, point N lies on side AB, and segments CM and CN are drawn from corner C. The visible top-left region is triangle DCM, bounded by DC, DM, and CM. Since AD is perpendicular to DC, the height of triangle DCM to base DC is DM. Inference: The square has side length 3 cm, so its area is 3 × 3 = 9 cm^2. The square is split into three equal-area parts, so each part has area 9 ÷ 3 = 3 cm^2. Triangle DCM is one of these parts, so (1/2)(DC)(DM) = 3. With DC = 3 cm, (1/2)(3)(DM) = 3, so DM = 2 cm.

Set area triangle DCM = (1/2)(DC)(DM) = (1/2)(3)(DM) = 3, giving DM = 2 cm.

method.method_draft: Set up coordinates from the diagram. Let A=(0,0), B=(3,0), C=(3,3), D=(0,3). Since M is on AD, write M=(0,t), so DM = 3 - t. From the text, the square area is 9 and the three regions are equal, so each has area 3. The image shows triangle DCM is one region; compute its area using coordinates/determinant with D=(0,3), C=(3,3), M=(0,t): area = 1/2 |3(3-t)| = 3(3-t)/2. Set this equal to 3, so 3 - t = 2. Hence DM = 2 cm.
